claims.text: Vietnam's time zone has the IANA name Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh, is UTC+07:00 all year and has no daylight saving time.
claims.source_hint: lab db: pg_timezone_names -> Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh|07:00:00|is_dst f; .NET 10 on host: BaseUtcOffset 07:00, SupportsDaylightSavingTime False

claims.text: The time in any time zone can be expressed as an offset from UTC, written after the time; +07:00 means the local clock is 7 hours ahead of UTC, so subtracting 7 hours gives UTC. A local time together with its offset identifies one instant.
claims.source_hint: refs/dotnet-docs docs/standard/datetime/time-zone-overview.md line 25; instantiating-a-datetimeoffset-object.md; time-demo: 06:20+07:00 -> 23:20+00:00

claims.text: ISO 8601 writes a date and time as the date, a T, the time and, to name one instant, the offset, as in 2026-03-31T06:20:00+07:00; without the offset the same text has no time zone information and is only a local time.
claims.source_hint: refs/dotnet-docs .../base-types/standard-date-and-time-format-strings.md lines 255-267 ("o", ISO 8601: offset, Z, or no zone for Unspecified)

claims.text: placed_at is a timestamptz column; for timestamp with time zone PostgreSQL converts an input with an explicit offset to UTC and stores the UTC instant, not the stated offset, so +07:00 and +00:00 forms of one instant store the same value.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs §8.5.1.3 Time Stamps (stored internally as UTC, zone not retained); db/schema.sql@stage-0 line 21

claims.text: Because Vietnam is UTC+7, every local time before 07:00 in Vietnam falls on the previous calendar day in UTC (orders 6 at 05:30 and 12 at 06:20 do; orders 7 at 07:45 and 3 at 08:05 do not).
claims.source_hint: Arithmetic from claim 2; db/seed.sql@stage-0 lines 26, 29, 30, 35; orders-by-day.sql output (second result: ids 6, 12)

claims.text: When a moment is read by more than one program or machine, keep it in UTC: in a timestamptz column such as placed_at (DateTime.UtcNow, not DateTime.Now) and in JSON between programs; an offset such as +07:00 also names the instant. Convert to local time only at the edge.
claims.source_hint: Outline item 2; refs/dotnet-docs docs/standard/datetime/converting-between-time-zones.md:23

claims.text: A timestamp (without time zone) column keeps only the date and time fields: PostgreSQL silently ignores any time zone indication in its input. A local time stored there, or as text without its offset, no longer says which zone it was written in.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs §8.5.1.3 Time Stamps (timestamp without time zone ignores zone indication)

claims.text: In a zone with daylight saving time, clocks change on set dates: at the move forward an interval of local time does not exist (invalid time), and at the move back an interval happens twice (ambiguous time).
claims.source_hint: refs/dotnet-docs docs/standard/datetime/time-zone-overview.md lines 31-43 (ambiguous time, invalid time, fixed/floating rule)

claims.text: DateTimeOffset holds a date and time together with its offset from UTC; TimeSpan.FromHours(7) gives the +07:00 offset.
claims.source_hint: .NET API docs DateTimeOffset, TimeSpan.FromHours; refs/dotnet-docs docs/standard/datetime/instantiating-a-datetimeoffset-object.md

claims.text: The "o" format writes a DateTimeOffset as ISO 8601 with its offset, seconds carrying seven fraction digits: the sample prints 2026-03-31T06:20:00.0000000+07:00, and after ToUniversalTime() 2026-03-30T23:20:00.0000000+00:00.
claims.source_hint: standard-date-and-time-format-strings.md 259-263 (fffffffzzz); dotnet run --project samples/DonHang.Samples -- time-demo, lines 1-2

claims.text: When you choose one form for your own data, choose UTC: with every stored time on the same clock, comparing two of them is easy, even for a person reading the digits.
claims.source_hint: Outline item 2; refs/dotnet-docs converting-between-time-zones.md:23 ("Converting individual time zones to UTC makes time comparisons easy")

claims.text: On .NET 10, TimeZoneInfo.FindSystemTimeZoneById accepts the IANA id Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh on Linux with time zone data, and on Windows when .NET uses ICU (not NLS or invariant globalization mode), as the sample is set up; TimeZoneInfo.ConvertTime gives the instant's time in that zone.
claims.source_hint: refs/dotnet-docs docs/core/whats-new/dotnet-6.md:264; docs/core/extensions/globalization-icu.md:34,136; DonHang.Samples.csproj@stage-0 (InvariantGlobalization false)

claims.text: The sample's last two lines print 2026-03-31 (the date in Vietnam, from ConvertTime) and 2026-03-30 (the date of UtcDateTime, which gives the same instant's date and time in UTC, as ToUniversalTime does).
claims.source_hint: time-demo at stage-0 (ff911b0), output lines 3-4; refs/dotnet-docs docs/standard/datetime/converting-between-datetime-and-offset.md:71-75 (UtcDateTime converts to UTC)

claims.text: For a timestamptz value, placed_at AT TIME ZONE 'zone' gives its local time in that zone as a timestamp without time zone, and date(...) keeps only the date part.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs §9.9.4 AT TIME ZONE; §9.9 date(timestamp) / cast to date

claims.text: Some conversions use the machine's own time zone, for example DateTime.ToLocalTime, so the result depends on where the code runs, and a machine's time zone is one of its settings.
